Gergeti Trinity Church

A 14th-century church at 2,170 m with Mount Kazbek behind it — the single most recognisable view in Georgia.

Time needed
3 h
From Tbilisi
160 km · 3:10
Road
Mostly paved
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
May–October
Entry
free

Gergeti Trinity is the image Georgia is known by. The church stands on an isolated summit above Stepantsminda at 2,170 metres, with the 5,054-metre cone of Mount Kazbek rising behind it. When the cloud clears and the glacier appears, the view really does look the way it does in photographs, which is not always true of famous places.

The church was built in the 14th century and has a separate bell tower, both in undecorated mountain stone. Its position was strategic rather than scenic: in times of invasion, relics from Mtskheta and Tbilisi were carried up here, because an attacking force could not realistically reach the summit.

There are two ways up:

  • On foot from Stepantsminda through Gergeti village — one and a half to two hours of steady climbing, roughly 500 metres of ascent
  • By car on the narrow concrete road, resurfaced in recent years — steep, effectively single lane, with tight hairpins and few passing places

Behind the church, trails continue towards the Gergeti glacier and the Sabertse ridge. Those are full mountain hikes and need a separate day, plus proper footwear. The church is active, monks live here, and services are held regularly, so it is not simply a viewpoint.

Practical advice

Kazbek is often hidden in cloud; your best chance is between seven and ten in the morning, after which cloud usually builds. Dress rules apply — headscarf and long skirt for women, long trousers for men, with wraps by the door. The wind at the top is constant and the temperature is five to seven degrees lower than in the village, so a jacket is necessary even in July. Facilities are minimal and there is no café, so buy water and food below. The nearest ATM is in central Stepantsminda.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Head north from Tbilisi on the Georgian Military Highway through Zhinvali, Ananuri, Pasanauri and Gudauri, over the Jvari Pass at 2,379 metres, then down through Kobi to Stepantsminda — 155 km and about three hours. From the village it is a further 6 km up a steep, narrow concrete road. A sedan can technically manage it in dry conditions, but a crossover or 4x4 is what you actually want, since passing an oncoming car means putting two wheels on dirt. In winter chains and four-wheel drive are essential. Fuel in Pasanauri or Stepantsminda.
